utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please. Unfortunately I gather we are not going to have access to LiveNote until it is fixed but I think it is important we proceed. Now I've just been proved to be a liar but there are some problems with it, I gather. Now, Madam, would you please stand up? And would you make the solemn declaration in the terms of the document which the court usher is showing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the name of God whom I respect, I make the solemn oath and I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Madam, sit down, please. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before I begin with this witness I just want to inform the Court and Mr. Domazet of a small matter or short matter that may have a Rule 68 implications. Over the weekend it was my first opportunity to speak with this witness. She informed me over the weekend that she made a statement to police authorities in Srebrenica so it may have some impact on the weight that the Court gives to Exhibits 59.1 and 59.2 and I make Mr. Domazet aware a so that he may question the witness if he wants regarding those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But have you given Mr. Domazet the statements she made?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He is in possession of all those statements and has been for sometime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. GROOME I'd ask that the witness be shown the pseudonym sheet. Examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What number are we up to in your list of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: 90, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, that will be Exhibit P90 and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. I'd ask you to take a look at the top line of the document that's before you, Prosecution Exhibit 90. Is that your name on that first line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. In the first line, as far as I can see -- ah, yes, up there, yes, you're right. I can see it. It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second line, is that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the purposes of concealing your identity we will refer to you as VG18 throughout the course of your testimony. I'd ask you if you need to refer to any of the people indicated on that sheet in front of that you please do so by using their number. Okay? I want to ask you, begin by asking you what village have you lived in for the last approximately 27 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Koritnik, 7 kilometres away from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what occupation were you engaged in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Housewife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what was your highest level of education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Muslim, Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the spring and early summer of 1992. Did there come a time when a number of people came to your house and inquired about your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Approximately before the departure and you said before April, before the departure in June, they came to look for my husband, and take him to our local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: There was Radomir, they called him Mica, his nickname, Milorad. I can't remember but, yes, Milorad, and they called him Mica, his nickname was Mica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many people altogether came inquiring about your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, they came, six or seven of them, said that they hadn't just come to call my husband to go to Prelovo, that they had come to call two others and that we had to sign that we had to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell them about where your husband was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: That he was looking after the live stock in the woods. He knew the man. But that was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these people that came to your house, did they go with two men from your village to Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Only after my statement. Then they said that I could call Osman Kurspahic and Redzo Memisevic and I volunteered to go and fetch my husband and stay with the cattle but they said no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did these two men go to Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I went and found them working in the fields and I said that I told them what Micun had said that they were to go to Prelovo and they said where is my husband, why didn't I send them? I explained and they had to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they given assurances that they would be safe on the trip to Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that they would go with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when these two men that you mentioned returned from Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, by my house, and they called them and told me not to call them any more ever again, but I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "them" are you referring to Osman Kurspahic and Redzo Memisevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. They provoked them there, saw people they didn't know with beards, things like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how much time transpired between the time these men left Koritnik and they returned from Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, you're asking a little too much of me but I think four or five hours, perhaps, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they returned, did Osman Kurspahic tell you what occurred in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that he signed, it was a Thursday, and that we had to be ready all on the Sunday to go to Visegrad, that he had signed and that we would be exchanged either in Kladanj or Olovo

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he tell you how he was treated in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time after that that a person by the name of [redacted] came and spoke with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He did, and before that, too. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around this particular point in time, can you tell us when it was that he came and spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He came when we were to go the last time and when I took out my things to Ljubisav Grujic and Dusan, I wanted to leave some of my things there and they promised, and he noticed that and he came in front of the door and said, "Where is my machine-gun?" And I said, "Over there." I built my own house, it has three floors. "Here is your machine-gun, I don't need a machine-gun," because I knew all those children and I protected them like I did my own. I lived with them for 27 years. And never exchanged any bad words. We celebrated Christmas and Bajram together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact have a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, no, no, never had a pistol. What would I need that for? Of course not. Nobody dealt with things like that. I didn't even have anybody in the police force, if a forestry man came or a policeman, I saw that in all my 27 years, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic, what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he hold a political position that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, no. His mother had divorced his father. He lived in Saban, that's where he was brought up. When the war broke out in Zadar, he fled to his father and that's what it was like, his behaviour towards us and the other neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the point in time you're having this conversation with him, did he make any statement regarding where you should go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, no. What he said was he told me that if my husband doesn't find the machine-gun, they would kill us. And my husband heard all this. He was hiding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the last night you spent in your house in Koritnik, do you recall that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, yes, I remember. Why not? Yes, I remember. It was by my house. That's what he said to us. We couldn't sleep. He said he would kill us but he didn't want us to leave a stench there. But when we go down there, probably he meant Visegrad, and we couldn't sleep because from April to our departure we weren't allowed to sleep in the house because if we were in the house, me and my (redacted) and my son, my husband had to stand guard over us but for a time, we didn't dare. We had a raspberry plot outside the house and that's where we slept there not inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just referred to a statement that Mr. Gavrilovic stated or said to regarding that he would kill you. I Would ask you to say exactly what he said to you using the words that he used, please

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: That's what he said, that's what he said to us, what I've just told you. That's what he said. That he didn't want us to leave a stink there, but when we go down, that he would do it. He didn't say where, he didn't mention Visegrad, but I think he meant Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the day, as best you can remember, that you left Visegrad for the last time, I mean, sorry, left Koritnik for the last time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, only when I die and close my eyes then I won't be able to but now I can of course, that was the 14th of July. I left my beautiful house at 6.30. How wouldn't I be able to remember my lovely native village?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you say it was the 14th of July. Was it also a Muslim holiday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was the 4th day of the Kurban Bajram holiday, and Kurban is the day I remember we didn't slaughter a sheep in memory of my father-in-law who had died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that have been the ordinary custom that you would have done on Kurban Bajram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, that was our tradition. We slaughtered a sheep for the dead for fathers, dead fathers and mothers, and if you had the wherewithal and means you would do this for your whole family, but usually it was your nearest and dearest, your mother and father if you were able to, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without telling us the name of any person, did you in preparation for leaving did you give some of your possessions to a Serb neighbour that you trusted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took out what I could because they promised, but when I left, and turned around to look at my house and leave my house, I didn't take anything out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- which of your possessions did you give to this neighbour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, what I could take, a chest, a fridge, a cooker, a mower and of course when I left, I took the car keys, the car stayed in the garage but I just handed them the keys, and handed over the keys to my house to those people. I didn't lock my house because I thought that I would come back there, so I didn't lock my house up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you left this morning, did you believe that you would return to Koritnik one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I still think so today. I think that today, too. Because if you collect all those animals up who did all those things, then I would return tomorrow. My two houses, my plot of land, and everything else. I have to go back because I have nothing to live for. I don't have a pension. My husband hasn't got a pension. We live -- we are on Serb land and in a Serb house and we live out of the small plot of land we farm there, and the whole of eastern Bosnia is empty. There are no Muslims in 1992 and 1993, none of the Muslims stayed there. They all had to leave. And especially us, across the Drina, over the Drina is our mother and Visegrad is too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Drawing your attention back to this morning of the fourth day of Kurban Bajram, did you assemble with other members of the village to leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. My husband heard from his father who went to the woods and stayed alive so he called us and our son to go, but I didn't want to leave my people, and he is safe there when he was alone because if there were more of us, it would make things more difficult, if you were to come across anyone, meet anyone, you would be suspicious. So for his own safety and security, I decided to leave with my own people. There were some 40 of us who left from the village. There were perhaps 25 houses, 25 households. I don't know the exact number, but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband want you to not go to Visegrad that morning but to go with him, flee with him, into the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes and not only that morning but before, too. He called me to go through the woods to Zepa with him before as well, that we should take to the woods and go to Olovo for instance or further on to search for free territory, but for his own security and safety, it was safer for him to go with another man rather than go with a woman, to go with me, because it was all territory that was not free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your husband have a son at that time, a young son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, I did. He was young. He was a frail boy. He suffered from tonsillitis and those three months it kept raining. It was very cold weather and the Serb children had taken his bicycle and they were riding it by our house. And we had to put on heavy clothing and take to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss with you are husband whether you are son would go with your husband into the woods or go with you and leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He did call him. He told the child -- he wanted to take the child but I couldn't separate myself from the child. And that's what it's like today. We spent the whole war alone and together. We were in Visegrad, Zepa, Srebrenica, Tuzla, Visoko, and when in 1996, or whenever the integration was, I came to Sarajevo and I had a daughter and son who were studying at university.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had this discussion with your husband, did your husband speak with a Serb person living in Koritnik and ask him to do something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did he speak with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. The one that we took the things to, because he was always a good person, but he didn't dare and I hid at his place with my son. But later on, he said he didn't dare harbour us any more and said that we would have to find another place to hide because he didn't dare because of the authorities who noticed that he was protecting us and because our children and his children were the closest of friends. They were inseparable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did your husband ask this man to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: My husband asked him to go with us down there to where we were supposed to go, because he said a bus would be waiting for us and he said, "Go with them, please, go with the two of them, and accompany all the people." Because this man said that they would kill all of them but not up here, down there, when they get down there, and he said that he wasn't working, on duty, that day, otherwise he was in the police force, but he said he was on duty that night and not during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Serb neighbour that your husband spoke with was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. That other one who told us, he told them -- the neighbour told my husband. It wasn't that one. It was the other one who said he would slaughter us all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He was a policeman the one who said he would kill us, yes, that's right. That's right. He can't be a mister, he can't be a mister, a gentleman, no, this man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I have missed it but what is the significance of her husband? Is he of a different ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your understanding regarding where you were to get the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Greben, perhaps two kilometres away from our village, the place was called Greben.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go to Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, my husband asked the neighbour and he took an automatic rifle and started out with us because the column had already left. It had gone on ahead so my husband asked him to accompany us there. And when we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. said goodbye to my husband, he went to the woods, and we left and I said to my son, "I don't know when we'll see him again."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Greben were there other villagers from Koritnik already assembled there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: They were waiting for us. We arrived in the village, the Serb village, and I reached my neighbour's and then we all moved off in the same column and Dusan went with us, behind us, and the column moved on ahead. And halfway between our village and Greben, (redacted), a Volkswagen came up and Ilija Gavrilovic came and that other man Dragomir, Gavrilovic his surname is too, and he put out his hand and made the sign that we should go down there and the other one pulled his hand into the car, Ilija, whereas he had showed us by his giving us a sign with his hand that we should go on and we went towards Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're making a waving motion with your hand; is that correct? Is that what he did that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, that we should go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Greben approximately how many people from Koritnik were there, altogether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: When we arrived there, at the place we were supposed to get into the buses, there were only the people from our village there, because that was a Serb village, so it was only the people from our village who had been expelled and there was another village that remained above us, two hours away on foot. I didn't hear them leaving, but from Prelovo and from that region, all of us were there, there were no more Muslims left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Muslim residents from Koritnik were assembled in Greben at that time, when you arrived in Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, about 40, 45, 47, I don't know the exact number. Don't hold me to the number because it was ten years ago, so I can't give you an exact figure, but thereabouts, quite certainly there were more than 40 of us. The whole settlement, all the households, everyone. We were there. There was a family called Ajanovic, Memisevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without telling us the names of all the people that were there, I'd ask you were those people, were they all civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all civilians, nothing but civilians. They all were retired and lived on off a pension and farming, just pensioners and farmers. Nobody had anything to do with anything. Nobody was a member of an army of any kind. They were all people 50, 55 and over. There were some women, because the ones that might have been members of some organisation, Kurspahic for example, they were taken away from their workplace and they worked there with us. If you want I can enumerate their names, but their wives and children were with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a young baby among the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, 48 years old (sic). She was born in the woods. She hadn't been washed yet, bathed or cleaned. The -- her mother either. We were all women, all mothers. We knew what was to be done but she had just given birth and had to go down from the woods some 10 kilometres to join us and then 7 kilometres more to Visegrad, and the woman was perhaps 17. She spent two days in labour in the woods giving birth. There was no other way out for us. That was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you to please just tell us again the age of the baby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: 48 hours old. On that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Greben, did you wait for a bus that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, we did. The army came by wearing uniforms. They were young soldiers, they asked us what are we waiting for, where are we going? We said, "We are waiting for the buses and we are going to Kladanj or to Olovo," and they said that Kladanj was in Serbia and that that's where we were going. They mistreated us that way. And some of the people who were there were our children's schoolmates and they asked where Kurspahic was. They were actually schoolmates but they had turned wild.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a bus ever come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Never, never. We called them up on the phone from a Serb house belonging to Slavka Gavrilovic, a little further off, half a kilometre in front. There were some people, Kurspahic and this person Dusan, but not -- no buses because as soon as we reached the -- our destination we saw that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did there tomorrow a time when you left Greben in the direction of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. This Dusan asked Micun, Milorad, to accompany us to the Banja, to go with us. And he took a rifle and he set off with us as far as Sase, also known as Banja, a spa, on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the place that you're referring to as Sase or Banja, is that where the road that you were on intersects with the road that goes up to the Vilina Vlas hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that location, did you see any people in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The military police. They identified everyone there, asked for ID cards. And we saw soldiers down there in a house, I forget the name of that man, they called him Crni. We saw a lot of soldiers because his wife was with -- very close to me but she never cast a glance at me and she didn't even come out. This house was on the other side of the road and there were a lot of soldiers but they didn't do anything to us. It was only the police who were asking where we were going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did one of the policemen say something to you regarding the fact that you had men and boys among your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Because I don't know his name but I know that he is a school mate of our children because they would pass through our village for eight years going to school and there were girls in our village so they knew each other from dances, from parties, and I can't remember the name of this girl. Any way, he came up to this girl and said, "I understand you women going, but where are these men going?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else regarding whether the men and boys should go to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. He just said that all sorts of things were going on in Visegrad but I don't know, I don't remember. He may have said something but I do apologise if I leave something out because ten years is a long time, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point in time, did some people who lived in Sase join the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The (redacted), Meho, his wife, Murka and Kurspahic, Igbala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the group then continue on to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, we did, from there we went on alone. This one said goodbye to us, he had to go back on duty, guard duty in Kamonica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say this one, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I'm referring to Milorad, Micun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you arrived in Visegrad, where was the first place that you went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We went to the police, the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the police station, the SUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, it used to be called SUP. It's always ours. It's still ours. I can't say it's anyone else's. My home is not [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened when you were at the SUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Osman Kurspahic went with a man of 25 to 30, a man in uniform, a policeman, I don't know him. I didn't dare look. And he said, "Who had called you?" And this Osman Kurspahic said that we had set off to be exchanged, to Kladanj or Olovo, and he said, who had called us? And they said, the Red Cross, and then he told us that the Red Cross was at the hotel at the Drina, that we should go there but that we should not take the main road but another road along the Drina River where the trucks, road used by trucks, and that we should go in a line two by two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Line 6 of the current page -- I finally got the transcript up on my screen -- should the reference the last word, be redacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person that you're telling us instructed you to go to the hotel, was this the person who came out of the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, he came out of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your understanding of why you should walk by the river two by two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you arrive at the hotel or did you go to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the hotel that's near the old bridge in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened after you arrived at this hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I can. When we arrived there, it was a large group and then Osman Kurspahic went inside again and again he came out with a young guy, if I can call him that. He was also in uniform. And he said, why hadn't we come earlier? Because six buses had left and I don't know how many trucks, that they had gone for Olovo or Kladanj, I don't know which, and why hadn't we come earlier? What are we going to do with you now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a young man. Can you give us his approximate age, as best as you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, like the Judge over there in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you want my age?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you take judicial notice of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I just look old, that's all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: About 30, I don't know. I didn't dare look. You're asking me too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now I do feel --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Because one didn't dare look to see, maybe it's hard for you to believe, all you had to do was look in front of you and listen to what was being said to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about the uniform that this person was wearing? Can you describe it as best you're able?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Black, black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this person wearing anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: A cap, like a beret. The policeman's cap, something like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about the colour of that cap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't remember. Of course, the same colour as the suit he wore but I don't know. I didn't look. It didn't interest me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've said -- you testified that this man told you that you had missed the buses that morning. Did he tell you when the next buses would arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. He did, yes. That we hadn't come on time, that we should go back to Pionirska Street, up there, that meant for a kilometre or more back, and that in the evening and the next day, buses would come to pick us up, that we should be there between 8.00 and 12.00 so that we would leave like the prefer convoy had left at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you told to go up to Pionirska Street, to stay there the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We were told to go to Pionirska Street, to go there, to all the Muslim houses are empty up there, but that's what we were told. If I've left anything out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think there was something suspicious about being directed up to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because there were Muslim houses nearby. My brother's house. He had an apartment. He had left a long time ago, already in May. When I passed by, I saw the curtains in my brother's apartment still hanging, and as soon as they told us to go back to a suburb, this Pionirska Street was in a suburb, we immediately found that suspicious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from your brother's apartment were there other Muslim houses or apartments that you were aware of that were vacant right in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. They were all. Maybe only ten per cent of the Muslims were still around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how far away was your brother's apartment from the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, between the hotel and my brother's apartment, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: [redacted]. I passed by it again on the way back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go up to Pionirska Street as you were instructed to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Where else? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to get up there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We were tired, wet through from the rain. It took us an hour to get there, and dragging our bags as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the way up, do you recall seeing any houses that you knew belonged to Muslims burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I saw, when I was approaching the town, the house of our doctor, Safet, I don't remember his surname, that it was burnt to the ground and some others, but I didn't pay attention because this was ordinary by then. Everything was burning except for our village while I was still in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if you were escorted by any Serbs on the trip from the hotel up to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. There was no one, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at Pionirska Street, was there a woman among your group that suggested that the group spread out and find different places to stay that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: From our column, because I was at the back of the column, I had five bags and my child was tired, and then one of my neighbours said that she should go and look up her uncle. They were there. That we should spread out, that she should go and stay with them and she said to her mother, "Look after the children I'll go and check whether they are in the house and I'll come out and meet you." And that was her suggestion that we go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did she suggest that you spread to several houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: For safety sake because we had heard from others, from before, that it will be better not all of us to be together in one group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when she returned from going up to speak with her relatives on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: She didn't have anyone to talk to. She came back immediately and told us -- not to everyone, but I was going with her mother-in-law and her children and she said that her uncle and aunt had been killed, that they were covered with blankets in the house and she started crying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the approximate age of her uncle and aunt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. They were our neighbours from our village. But he had a house in Pionirska Street where his sons lived but he used to live with us in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his approximate age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Maybe about 65 or 70. She was younger, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there then come a time when the group gathered by the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. We stopped there. I knew the house. The teacher of my children, Dennisa Karcic used to live there until she built her own house and I used to visit her so I knew the house. All those houses were vacant. We didn't enter. We stood there, and that is when Mitar Vasiljevic appeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately what time of the day is it when this person you're referring to as Mitar Vasiljevic was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: About 3.00, half past three, I don't know exactly. It could have been around that time. If you want the exact time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person you're referring to now before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. I knew his wife as a very fine woman. She worked at the Banja as a sales woman. She was a very fine person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was her name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Milojka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn the name of this person that you're referring to now as Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We were looking around what to do, and I saw him shaking hands with (redacted), and this one said to him, "How are you Mitar? Where have you been, Mitar?" And so we turned around. I may have seen him before, because he used to work as a waiter, so maybe I saw him sometimes with my son and daughter but I didn't remember, no, because we were very frightened when we got there. And so he himself said he was Mitar Vasiljevic and that he was coming on behalf of the Red Cross to put up the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe you would recognise this person if you saw him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I could. Only once I die I would no longer be able to recognise. But when I see someone once, I can, yes. And even then, I -- he's over there. There he is. Of course I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise him in the courtroom here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe who you're referring to now by telling us where this person is sitting and what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Here, or when he was in our place, in Visegrad? I can. He's sitting to my left. I didn't look really to see how he's dressed. Of course he's in black, but I don't even want to look at him, because he didn't keep his word. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look now and be certain of what you're testifying to. Is the person that you're referring to now in this courtroom the person that you saw that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I can. He's behind this man here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: It's not black. It's brown, I think. I can't see too well at a distance. It's brown, brown. Only he's ten years older now. He looked better in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record note that the witness has identified the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The transcript will, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now would you describe for us what he was wearing back on this day, this day on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He had black clothing, a black coat right down to the ground, a hat with a feather in it, as if he was in the movies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe more specifically what you mean by "as if he were in the movies." What type of movie did this hat remind you of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, like a man as -- he wasn't like the usual people in uniform, but please don't tie me with these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're just asking you to the best of your recollection to describe what you remember. Do you remember the colour of the hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Was it black like his suit? I don't know. I wasn't even looking. I was looking around what to do, I didn't even look at him, to tell you the truth. It must have been the same colour as his suit, black. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Mitar Vasiljevic addressed the group of people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. He shook hands with Mujo and he addressed us too, saying he was Mitar Vasiljevic, that he was accommodating refugees on behalf of the Red Cross, and that we should feel free and safe, and that we should all be in one group, and that no one may touch us and no one would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by that, "should remain as one group." Can you tell us exactly what he said regarding that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: That we shouldn't part, that we should all stick together. There were persons who had their sons' houses in town and they thought they would go there, but he told us to stay together. So we were a bit uncomfortable about it, but still we stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you saw him write something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He took out a notebook pad and he wrote down something. I didn't know what he was writing. He was writing a certificate that we would be safe there, that no one would hurt us there, and he gave it to (redacted). And he came in last, (redacted), and he showed us this piece of paper and said, "This is what Mitar Vasiljevic gave me."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mitar Vasiljevic explain the significance of this piece of paper, or what it meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. He explained it to Mujo but not to us. He just said that we were safer there and if anyone should come to mistreat us, that we should show them this piece of paper, that we were legally there. That was our understanding and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give you any information regarding a bus the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He did, yes. That we would spend the night there and that the next day, we should go down there to the bus, where the bus would come to pick us up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without telling us the name of your brother or where he worked, did you at some point have a discussion with Mitar Vasiljevic regarding your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I did. When he said that he was a waiter from the new hotel, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: [redacted] Maybe he'll remember saying that to me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he correct about where your brother was working at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Mitar Vasiljevic spoke to the group, did he have an additional conversation with Mujo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. We entered, so we believed him that we would be safe, that he was a person responsible for refugees. He gave us this piece of paper. And I don't know anything more. I didn't see him again there. I went inside. Perhaps you can ask me more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mujo go inside at the same time that you went into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He followed us. He was carrying a small glass of brandy, saying that Mitar Vasiljevic had given it to him, and he was carrying this piece of paper as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how much time transpired between the time you went into the house of Jusuf Memic and Mr. --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, this was immediately, one after another. We weren't standing around in the street. He came very shortly after us, immediately after us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point in time, would it be fair to say that most of the people from Koritnik were now inside the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. All the people who had lived in Koritnik, everyone, except my husband. All the others were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to you look at that sheet of paper down in front of you and I want you to look at the name next to VG101. Without saying that person's name, was that person in the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to look at the name above that, VG78. Was that person also in the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the point in time when you enter the house of Jusuf Memic, after receiving the certificate, did there come a time when other men came to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how much time transpired between your entering the house and these men arriving at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: About an hour later. We were praying to God, having lunch, about an hour later, a little less. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was your belief that this was connected to Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know. When Mitar Vasiljevic was there, I didn't see anyone else. Now, whether he sent someone, I don't know. I have come here to tell you about what I saw with my own eyes. Now whether he sent someone, let him tell, let him say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you learn the identity of any of the people that came to the house at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. How could I, for heaven's sake? You don't dare look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the men that came at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, they came before. There were some that came before, and they said, "You and you, there is a corpse near the Drina." This was before. "There is a corpse that needs to be buried. You and you, there is a body near by in Potok." So these men who had come with us, Kurspahics, they went to bury those bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some of the people in the group know these men who came to the house at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: You mean to take them off to dig the graves? Those people? I didn't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the men that came to the house after Mitar Vasiljevic gave you the certificate. How many men came to the house at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic came with the people. He introduced himself. I wouldn't have recognised him but he introduced himself and said he was Sredoje Lukic and two other people came with him, came to our house, an hour, an hour and a half later. So let's go on to that now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you learn the names of those other people that were with the person who identified him as Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: When the people left, when they finished all their business, then the others recognised him, I didn't, and told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who did they tell you these people were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: There was Laco and Milan Lukic, Laco, as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Laco, was there anybody else with these me at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well there were people around the house. You could hear voices but only the three of them went into the house whereas the others were standing round the house and you could hear them talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this day, had you seen any of these men before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: You mean the one that went -- the one that came into the house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As best you're able to describe, can you tell us what these men were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, they were in uniforms. They had uniforms on. They had rifles. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I neglected to ask you a question regarding Mitar Vasiljevic. The first time you saw him, was he armed with any weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't even look when I was talking to my brother -- about my brother, I don't know. I can't say whether he had or didn't. I don't know. I don't know. I can't say. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened inside the Jusuf Memic house after these three men entered the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us the first thing that happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Let me take a rest, please. They came to the house and this one introduced himself, saying he was Sredoje Lukic and he said that we should all go into one room. And cash, he wanted cash, money and gold. And he said, "If I find a single dinar on anyone after that," and he pulled out a knife of some kind from his boot, and he flashed it around and said, "If I find a penny on anybody else, I will use this -- strip you naked."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We all went into this one room and put our -- took our money out and gold, jewellery. We all put it out on the table. And Laco then went into another room, he sat down, he had his rifle here, he made the sign of three, telling three people to come in, and the three of us went in and then he said, "Take your clothes off."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you among the first to go into that room, that second room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. I was in that first group. I was with those first people. I was always together with them. And I was -- when he said, "Three of you come in," I was with those three. He was sitting down and he said, "Take your clothes off." And I started unbuttoning my jumper. I unbuttoned it and I unbuttoned my blouse and I said I wasn't going to do anything -- any more, and he said, "Take your clothes offer," like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're holding up your finger did he hold up his finger and make any reference to his finger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: This is what he showed me. He said that I should be as naked as this finger here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: And then I started taking off my underwear, my bra, and underwear, and came and stood in front of him and went round in a circle and he asked me where my husband was and I said my husband had gone to Montenegro because that's what this other man Mica, nicknamed Mica, told me, Milorad his name was. I'm going back a little. And he said, "Why didn't [redacted] go?" My husband, and I said, he didn't dare. And he asked me where my husband was? And I said, "Went to Montenegro to work." And he said he was gone to Gorazde to deal with our women there and he said no -- and I said, "No, he's gone to Montenegro to work like he does every season, every year." And he said, "Put your clothes on." And I put my clothes on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us just the first name of the other two who were in the room with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I see the name here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then would you refer to it, refer to that person by number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Number 78.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there two people in that group with the same name, with that name, of VG78?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, with the same name, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who was in the room with you, what is her approximate age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: She was born in 1968. I know that. Together with my daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the approximate age of the other person with the same name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: She has two children, three children, that is, she had three children, and her husband was taken away, also [redacted], before we left. She was 27 years old or thereabouts, she's still a young woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did one of the two women that was in that room with you refuse to get undressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. Number 78.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when she refused to get undressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: She was with me. She said that she wasn't going to get dressed and -- get undressed and that he could kill her. But this other person held her and I unbuttoned her clothing and we took her clothes off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the people in the room that or in the house that day -- at that time searched in a similar manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: The women, the three of us women, were there and then there was another empty room and then the next three came in and experienced the same thing we did, all of them, every single one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take for all of the people in the house to be searched in this manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was fairly fast, perhaps an hour, an hour and a half, I don't really know. When they left, it was still day light. It wasn't dark yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that this occurred, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic inside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see him in the house. I can't say that. But there was somebody outside because when we were in the room, it was not so -- it was quiet and we could hear them talking, somebody talking outside the house, but he wasn't in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After all of the people in the house had been searched, did these three men leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. They searched everyone, looked in the children's pockets. And a little boy, whose father had been taken off, he didn't know, and the women put a lot of money into the children's pockets. They put money into [redacted] pockets too and the child didn't see that somebody had put some money in his pocket. I don't know how much there was. Two million, I think, then Sefer and Milan found the money and hit him like this. And Osman Kurspahic said, who was his [redacted], said, "Don't touch the child," and he said, "I'll touch you too in a minute." And that's what happened. The others were with the men over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've just indicated what he did by holding a fist up to the side of your head. Is that what that person did? You need to answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were describing what this person did, you held your right hand in a fist up to the side of his head. Is that what this person did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he did. He hit the child, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now before they left, did one of these men say something to the group regarding where they were going and what they were going to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: After that, they collected the money, put it in a bag, and the jewellery in another bag, filled the bags up, especially the money, and when they searched everything, they said, "You in the leather jacket, and you, Vila come out." That's what Sredoje Lukic said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were they talking to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, they told Jasmina Vila and a young woman who was pregnant. She was very young, though. She was 17, perhaps. They said, "You in the leather jacket and you, Vila," because he knew Vila from before, "you go out."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had this person you referring to as Jasmina Vila stayed in your house just before this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, and she started off with us from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while she was in the Memic house, did she make an attempt to try to hide her face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, she hid her face when she went after us, she put a scarf around her face like this. She prepared the uniform for an elderly person and that's what she did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did these men leave with these two young girls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those girls return at some point to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how much time transpired between the time they left and the time they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Half an hour perhaps, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition of these two women when they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, I can't describe it. They looked terrible. The mother and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. father-in-law of this one were there and the other was a girl. She wasn't a woman. I can't describe it. They looked terrible. They had changed a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what, if anything, you noticed different about their clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was different about their clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know how to describe it. I can't. I can't describe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe their emotional state at the time they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: They were abused. Somebody had said something to them but they didn't dare tell us what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were either of these women crying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, this one, the one that had her in-laws there. She cried a lot. It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the men left the house, did they say anything regarding the safety of the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: They said, "Well, we didn't do anything to you. We are going to get" -- "collect two sheep, take two sheep away and eat them. And we've earned a lot of money." That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the men return a second time or another time that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, of course they did. Had they not come, I wouldn't be here to start off with. I would be in my own house with my own people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this next time that they arrive at the house, is it dark at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Dark, night, yes. It was perhaps half past 10.00. The children had gone to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us or describe for us what happened to make you realise that they had returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, we heard a car coming up. And there was the kind of noise that when you didn't have an exhaust pipe on the car. You could hear the car coming. We saw them moving up our street because we were right by the street, and when they turned, the lights of the car hit our windows and lit them up and one of the women said, Kurspahic said, "They are going to kill us now or strangle us. Or set light to us."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people returned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. Was that a correction?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what she said? I didn't understand whether she said strangle or light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask to you repeat what you just testified this other person said when they approached. What exactly did she say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: When they came in front of our house, whether I said anything or not, but the person lived in a village by the Drina, not far from us and there were several cases there. And she went into town and learnt of things like this and as soon as the car came in front of the door and our windows, she probably, whether she heard or what, but she said, "They are going to kill us or set fire to us."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Approximately how many people returned to the house at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: One of them came to call us but we heard more of them downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We jumped up straight away and saw that something was wrong. The children were still sleeping. My child was still asleep. And he came to the door and said, "You have to leave. You have to go away from here. You're not safe here. The Green Berets are shooting up there from Babin Potok. You're on the road here, on the line of fire. So you have to leave. We can't look after you here." That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person you're referring to as "he," do you know the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know. Had I known his name, I would tell you now, but I don't. He was wearing a uniform and the people who took away our gold and money, those -- it was organised. It wasn't done by one man. It was done by a group of men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of the same people who had come earlier in the day and took the gold and money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: While they were talking, I noticed that it was probably those people because nobody knew about us but them. But I can't say I actually saw them. I jumped up, got my child, and carried out the order, got my things together, got my child. He said we should leave our things there and that we could come back for them tomorrow morning but that we should go towards this destination where we were going, that we should leave straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this person made a reference to the Green Berets, did you take that to mean that they were saying Muslim forces were attacking the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: We got ready and the people started leaving towards this destination point. I stayed on last. I put -- I dressed my child, got my things and started off. The man went behind me and I saw the others along the road, you could see a little bit, but then they turned the lights, the car lights off. I didn't dare look around much but I saw that there were some people over there but I didn't look to see who it was. And when I got down there, they had already boarded, and I saw -- I heard the stories of the women who had been brought there before us, for example [redacted] [redacted]. She went to stay with her daughter Jasmina and I heard that Jasmina was crying and there was a child crying, and she was quietening this two-year-old child down and I saw that something was very wrong. We were going down to the water, to the creek, and I knew that something was going to happen. And when I wanted to go in, he hit me with his butt in my back here and said -- he swore at our balija mother, and said, "Where is Alija now? Why doesn't he help you now?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few specific questions regarding the trip from the Memic house to this other place you're describing. You have told us that car lights were turned off. At the time you first left the Memic house, were there some car lights on at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, by the other houses, yes, where people lived, but our house there was no light inside or outside. You could just see a little from the other streets, from the light coming from the other streets where there was a little light, but I didn't dare look around. I just listened to the orders given us and did what I had to do. I didn't look around to see if there were any lights or not. He was right beside me and I didn't even raise my eyes to look at him. I wasn't interested. I thought they were taking to us a better destination than we were at that time. That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately what was the distance between the Memic house and this other house that you went into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. If you want me to be specific, I don't know. Perhaps 20 metres. I'd like to go and see the house again to see everything, rather than going back to my own one where I lived for 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you the last person to leave the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: The last, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you also the last person to enter this other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've described something being shoved into your back. Can you tell us in greater detail, if you're able, what it was that was shoved into your back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Well, the one walking beside me, he behaved in a proper and correct manner, until we got there. I couldn't go in because the house was full and then when I heard from the people who weren't with us, I knew that something was amiss, that there was some criminal acts going on, and that something was going to happen to us. So when I came to the door there, but not while I was walking, because I thought that what they said was true, that it wasn't safe where we were and that we had to be transferred to another place. That's what I actually thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did this person do to you as you were at the doorway of the second house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: He said, "Get in, balija" and then he cursed my mother and said where is Alija to help us now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he fire his weapon at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No, not then. When he shut us in, I wasn't able to go in because the house was full, so I was forced in, and then there was -- he shot a burst of gun fire in front of the door and opened the door again and said, "Listen, that's the Green Berets firing from up there." But we weren't mad. We knew what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, was there something shoved into your back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, a rifle. And even now, I can feel my body going numb where he did this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first went into that house, were you able to hear children crying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, the little baby that was 48 hours old, two days old, never stopped crying. And then I heard Jasmina's child, the two-year-old child, he kept crying. He was screaming and she said, told him to keep quiet. It was dark. There was shooting in front of the door. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest here is the place to pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume again at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness VG18, we left off at the point in time when you had just entered this second house. I want to ask you, from the time that the -- these men returned this night until the time that you were -- the time that you went into this second house, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I didn't see him, shall we say, in the house and on the road, because I didn't look around, but there were some soldiers down there who were talking and laughing, but I can't say that I spoke to him and that he was there. I didn't. But there were other men around the house so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier about some women who were not from Koritnik being inside this second house. Do you recall that? And I'd ask you not to mention their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Very well. [redacted] and some others with their children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know these others who were there with children. The house was packed full. I recognise some of the women by their talk. I didn't mention their names, only their surname. There were some, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look at that sheet of paper in front of you and draw your attention to VG87. Without mentioning any names whatsoever, surname or first name, was the wife of that person in this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the inside of the house for us, as best you're able?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I can't, because the door was shut. There was shooting. They cursed our mothers. I didn't look around. I just looked how I could save myself. It was like any big room, because there were a lot of people. It was as full as a match box. I could feel that I was stepping on people as I was trying to pass through and reach the window. Of course, there was furniture, when people were sitting around, and when the shooting was heard they started screaming, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the other people in the house say something regarding the floor of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I heard, afterwards, stories, but I don't know that. I was the last to enter. I was frightened. I wouldn't even be able to tell you exactly where my child was. I had lost control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you went into the house, did you hear anything about the floor of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes. They were saying that there was something sticky, that something had been done before the people got there, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to feel anything sticky on your feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I don't know. Everyone has his own opinion about these things. I've told you that there were so many people that I couldn't really reach the floor so I don't know. And we were frightened so I don't know. Please don't insist. I heard stories about that, that there was something, but I'm telling you what I myself experienced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you walked around the -- around inside this house, were your feet able to reach the floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: No. There were so many people, it was packed. I didn't move around. I saw the window immediately and headed towards it, and as I went there, I saw that there were some people there who hadn't been with us, who must have come before us, and that something was in the making.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear some of the people praying at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I did. That we should pray to God. My father was a religious man and he said one should pray to God but one should seek salvation, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join them in prayer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: Of course I did, but I was looking around how to save myself, and God did help me, helped some of us to save ourselves. But the most important thing is to try and save yourself, even though you pray to God.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened inside that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG18
utterances.text: I can. That's why I've come. To tell the truth about my people. When the door was locked and the shooting was heard, they were laughing outside the door. There were several voices and then they opened the door. And I was close to this [redacted] whose grandchild was crying, this baby. "Can I come up to you, [redacted]?" And she said "Do," and I was close by, and she was right next to the window. However, the door opened and as soon as the door opened, the flames shot up in different colours, blue, yellow, as if somebody was heightening the fire, and then the screaming started. I turned my head away from the smoke and I had reached the window. Then I put this hand over my mouth and I hit against the window. The window was covered with thick glass. I noticed this glass, it was reinforced. I turned around to look at it. I noticed it as soon as I went in, and I hit against the glass with this hand and held the other one to my mouth, and then the glass broke but in the way a windshield breaks, it didn't fall out. I couldn't pass. And I didn't know anything about my child. I couldn't pass. There seemed to be some wires that wouldn't let me pass. And just then, God saved me. My child pushed me. I fell and he fell on my back and he said, "Run. Run, mother" and when I turned around, I saw my neighbours with small children protecting them. They were screaming, each one of them had one, two or three, and then this baby and this little girl of nine, Sanisa, and the grandson, was on her lap screaming and I passed and jumped out and my son jumped on my back and he said, "Let's run, mother." I couldn't walk because a bomb was thrown into the other part, and the shrapnel hit me in my neck, not much because I was crouching. And these shrapnel were falling on my neck and head and hand and as I jumped, from the explosion I couldn't feel my body because, as I jumped I sort of felt as if half my face was missing and my son pulled me and said, "Let's run." And we ran down to the creek and we hid there and we -- as we were crouching there, there was a kind of flashlight lit up. They were already by the door. And when they saw that some people had jumped out, myself and my son and this person number 30, 80 and 13, 38 came out, they came after us. We reached the creek and then number 13 they caught her, and they wounded her and she stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
