utterances.text: And aside from soldiers from the Uzice Corps, did you see some other soldiers who you did not believe to be regular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. They were soldiers with long beards, they weren't clean-shaven, they were dirty. They looked sort of like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what -- how their age was in comparison to the soldiers from the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, they were over 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the soldiers in the Uzice Corps, what would have been their approximate age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: 20, 22 perhaps, thereabouts. Younger soldiers, quite a bit younger. And they looked better kept. Their hair was cut. They were shaved, shaven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe -- did the uniform of these unusual looking soldiers, was it the same or was it a different looking uniform from those you saw on the soldiers from the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the regular soldiers of the Uzice Corps more or less were wearing the same type of uniform. The others had similar uniforms because they came from the same direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what these soldiers did with respect to the people who came out of the forest and into the local community? What did these soldiers do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, two trucks turned up full of these soldiers and their guns were attached to the trucks. The people who were there in Brstanica, who had gathered in Brstanica were to move towards Visegrad, and the army came to provide security for them. So we were in Brstanica for half an hour. Two trucks came full of soldiers and took up their first positions. It belonged to part of the Visegrad municipality which had not yet been taken over by the army, which was not yet under the control of that army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the group of people in Brstanica go in the direction of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. They moved in the direction of Visegrad. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long was the column of people that went to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the column was over 1 kilometre long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there JNA trucks at the front and the rear of the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. In front of the column, the first truck went in front of the column with this cannon or gun connected to it and the same thing happened at the end of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the column reached the centre of Visegrad town, where did it go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: When we reached Visegrad, I wasn't able to recognise the town at all. It had nothing to do with the beautiful town that I had remembered. It was full of the military, tanks, trucks and other vehicles, all over the streets. They had just arrived from the direction of Dobrun Vardiste. They said things to us and by -- the older people did especially, but the people passed by those trucks and we managed to reach the Visegrad stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the stadium, were there people there already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. At the stadium, members of the White Eagles were already present, and they introduced themselves as members of the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you arrived, did additional people enter the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. There were quite a lot of people before we arrived and there were a lot that came after us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for us the number of people of Muslim ethnicity that had gathered in the stadium that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the stadium was full of people so that they were in their thousands, several thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers that you say introduced themselves as White Eagles, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: There were quite a number that were armed, and there were others who were not armed, but mostly they were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us specifically where in the stadium were they positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: They were positioned in the middle of the stadium where their leader was supposed to come and there were some also at the entrance gates to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from these White Eagles soldiers, were there also members of the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: At the stadium?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: At the stadium, there were mostly members of the White Eagles so I don't remember actually too well about JNA members. I just remember soldiers that were mostly wearing white belts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe any of the Muslim people attempt to leave the stadium after they had entered the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they permitted to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point, did somebody make an announcement using a megaphone and make an announcement to the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Crowd -- yes, he addressed the crowd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that person say over the megaphone to the crowd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: That their commander would come, the commander of the White Eagles, from Uzice, from Serbia actually. I apologise, from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he say how he would come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: In a helicopter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did a helicopter arrive soon thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Soon after that, the helicopter arrived, about 20 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did a commander come from or leave the helicopter and address the crowd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes. His soldiers took up positions in the middle of the stadium and the helicopter landed. And their commander came out and he addressed the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say something about the villages on the western or left bank of the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. He said on the left bank of the Drina all the people may go back home because his army had already cleansed the area; whereas the right bank of the Drina, people should not go back to, no one may go back to, until the next day and that we had to spend the night in the Drina hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which side of Drina is the -- is Koritnik, the right or left bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: The right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people searched at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, all the people were searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've just told us that the people were -- or some of the people were instructed to stay at the Drina hotel. Did you stay at the Drina hotel that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many nights did you stay at the Drina hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how many Muslims were in the hotel that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a number of our people there, but I could not tell you the number, because these were people from several villages on the right bank of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel safe there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We didn't feel safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why didn't you feel safe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We had no protection there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That night, were you able to hear gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was gunfire and no one could sleep. It was close by, the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that gunfire last throughout the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you eventually did return to the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you escorted by any members of the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the way back up to your village, did you see whether any houses belonging to Muslim people had been burnt on the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. Some Muslim houses had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you insulted by people of Serb ethnicity on the way back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, when we left town there were no insults by neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you returned to Koritnik, did you hear accounts of people being arrested and other houses being burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. My village is 7 kilometres from Visegrad, and the whole district counts some 30 villages, and all were burnt. My village and another village, only remained and it was their turn to evacuate. And one could see quite a lot of the burning and everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the second week of June in 1992 and ask you did there come a day when you saw a red van and a truck driving in the direction of the village of Musici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there something unusual about this red van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. This vehicle would move around the whole area, around all those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe this red vehicle for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. It's a vehicle that could take about six to eight passengers. And in whatever village it appeared, so it came to my village, two or three times, but the neighbours wouldn't let it come in. So it was turned back. The vehicle didn't have an exhaust pipe and it made quite a lot of noise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The neighbours that turned the red vehicle back, were they your Serb neighbours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after you saw this red vehicle and a truck driving towards Musici, did a person by the name of Jasmina Vila come and stay with you in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. She came the next day to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What village is she from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: From the village of Musici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did she describe for you what occurred in the village of Musici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, that day, the red van had come and all the men, about 20 of them, I am talking in approximate numbers because I don't know the exact number, they were called to attend some sort of a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: And then they all had to get on to the truck, there was no meeting, and they were driven off in an unknown direction so that several persons, Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic, and a girl whose name I don't know, took part in this as well as several other soldiers. That was what Jasmina Vila told us, who unfortunately is no longer alive. She lost her life in the fire in Pionirska Street, because she knew well, Sredoje Lukic, who had driven this vehicle seven days prior to this, and she had run away from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she describe being taken to the village of Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. Sredoje Lukic took her to his village, Rujiste, which is about 30 kilometres from Visegrad. What he did to her, she wouldn't say. She wouldn't tell me and my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you that she was afraid of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is why she came to my village, because her village, Musici, was right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when a Serb neighbour of yours in Koritnik came to your house and told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm afraid you've got so far ahead of the French translation that you're losing them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we slow down?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when a Serb neighbour of yours from the village of Koritnik came to your house and told you that you had to leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what day was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It was around the 11th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did that person say you had to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We were supposed to leave two to three days later. That no one could continue to guarantee our safety in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date on which you left the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who from your immediate family, without telling us their names, went -- left the village of Koritnik that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: My mother and father. And many relatives. My whole family, my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your understanding about where you were going that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We were told that we were going to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your father go in that -- with you in the direction -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No. A Serb neighbour told him to take to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your understanding of how you would get to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: By bus. That's what we were told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you to get on these buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: A place called Greben, 20 kilometres from Koritnik. Again, I'm giving approximate figures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you arrive in Greben that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. We arrived in Greben.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there buses there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave from Greben to go to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. We headed towards Visegradska Banja, the spa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after reaching Visegradska Banja, did you go on to the centre of Visegrad town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We were stopped there. There was their checkpoint there, the Serb checkpoint. Those people had no information about the people coming, and so they telephoned, they called up Visegrad, and the bus was standing at the widening of the road, on the side of the road, but there was no driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where precisely was the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Just behind the Serb checkpoint in Visegradska Banja, so there was the -- the road widened there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this area also known as Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left this area and continued on to the centre of Visegrad town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate for the Court when it was you arrived in Visegrad that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: So in Sase some more people joined us. I forgot to mention that. And we arrived in Visegrad at about half past twelve or 1.00 roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the first place that you went to when you arrived in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: To the SUP building of Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened at the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the guard came out. He had no information about us. He asked, "Who are you? What are you doing here?" And he said that they were not responsible for this. And he told us to go to the Red Cross, the new hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The new hotel, is that the hotel that's by the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and other members of the group go to the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, and we arrived in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when somebody came out of the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We arrived in front of the hotel and there too was a guard. He was armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: A dog started barking, belonging to one of my relatives, and he asked whose dog it was. And my relative said it was his, and he said, "Take him over there to the land" -- "plateau." He removed the rifle from his shoulder and he shot about ten bullets into that dog. The owner came back to join the group, and then he told others to pick up the dog and carry him to the old bridge and throw him away. However, these people said it wasn't their dog, and he said, "You go up there and I'll show you too." However, the older women managed to plead with him and they took the dog to the bridge and threw it over. So a person came out in front of the Red Cross, who didn't introduce himself. He spoke to the people from a distance of some ten metres, and again approximately, and the person said that the convoys had left at 12.00 and that we had to spend the night somewhere. And only the next day would there be a convoy for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you just a pull your chair in a little bit so you're closer to the microphone. Apparently they are having some difficulty hearing everything you're saying. Okay. Was anything said about where you should spend the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. In the Visegrad Mahala, that means the right bank of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Pionirska Street in the district of Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. It's also known as the Pionirska Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and other members of the group go up to Pionirska Street that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. All of us, we headed for the Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether or not you were accompanied by any Serbs on the way up to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how long was the group of people that travelled up to Pionirska Street that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It took about 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group of people that went up, was it one continuous group or were there gaps between some of the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: There were gaps, quite a lot, because people were carrying things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that some people were slower than others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to this area before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On approximately how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, maybe -- quite a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your reason for being in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I had some relatives there. I went to attend certain tournaments and with school there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the school that's up on Pionirska Street? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived on Pionirska Street, did you go to a particular house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person who owned that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I think the surname was Memic, Jusuf, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe what happened after you arrived at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: So I was towards the end of the column, and when we arrived in front of that house, a person arrived who exchanged greetings with (redacted) (redacted) and shook hands with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us how this person was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. The person had a suit, a camouflage -- it looked black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the person wearing anything on their head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, a hat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the hat in greater detail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, it was a long time ago. I can't remember, to be able to describe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what this person looked like, their approximate height, their approximate weight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. The person wasn't tall, rather short, rather heavy. The person was not armed. That's as much as I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time that you saw this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor showed you a set of photographs including pictures of 12 different men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise any of the people in that group of photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I wasn't able to recognise because there were several photographs that looked alike, so I did not recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were telling us about -- or telling us that this person approached Mujo. What is Mujo's last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted), from the village of Sase, who was with us in the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who spoke first, this person that you saw or Mr. (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: This person, because Mujo didn't have a voice. He didn't dare speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did this person say to (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He extended his hand and said, "Where have you been? How are you, Mujo?" And the answer was, "And how have you been, Mitar?" So I knew they were talking about a Mitar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea of where you were at the time Mujo and this person who Mujo referred to as Mitar, how far were you from these two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I was from between three to four metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to hear the conversation that occurred between them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It was a brief conversation, and that person then addressed all the people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present during that entire conversation between Mujo and this person Mujo referred to as Mitar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I was close by, close by. I was no longer interested in that, but I was very close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they finished their conversation, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He introduced himself to everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to say what -- when you say, "He" who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to use his words when you describe what he said. You said he introduced himself to everyone. Can you tell us exactly what it was he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: "My name is Mitar Vasiljevic. I represent the Red Cross. I am in charge of your accommodation and security."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He asked us whether we had settled down in the house. And as he saw that we were settled in, he said that we would be safe and secure. And that we had to spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He said that there would be a convoy the next day and that nobody would touch us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Then he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before he left, did he given anything to anyone in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, he did. I apologise. He did give something. He took out a note pad, a certificate, and wrote down something and gave it to (redacted) (redacted) so that if anybody would come and if anybody asked you who you are and what you are, you can show this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him writing on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do with it after he wrote on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He gave it to (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after he gave it to (redacted), did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it that he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: If anybody asks who you are and what you are, you can take out this certificate and show them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else before he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. He said that, "You'll have a convoy tomorrow, in the morning, early." And he said that nobody would harm us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this person left -- well, sorry. Were you able to see in what direction this person -- where this person went after they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this person left, did other people come to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. About 45 minutes to one hour went by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who came to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: A man whom many people knew in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen this man before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, no. That was the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Many of the people, my relatives, knew him and they called him by his name, Sredoje, Sredoje Lukic, so that I in fact saw that it was Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the first sign that you saw that people were coming back to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this person arrive on foot or were they in some type of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: They had their own vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe it for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: The people heard the vehicle. It didn't have an exhaust pipe, and you could hear it coming up the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever see the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It stopped in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of Sredoje Lukic's arrival or just prior to it, did you hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, there was shooting, yes, as they were going up the street in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the person you've referred to as Sredoje Lukic, were there other people with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: And there was another soldier, whom I didn't know, and several soldiers outside the house. They were outside. I couldn't see them. I just heard them. I just heard them joking around. They were taking out some girls, and joking, having a laugh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how Sredoje Lukic was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform. He had a sniper rifle, knife. He didn't have a cap on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us how Milan Lukic was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: The same way, the same clothing. He had an automatic rifle, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to this day, had you seen the person you're referring to as Milan Lukic before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how is that you learned his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, many of my relatives knew both of them, neighbours, so that they called them by their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a question and I'd just asked you to repeat your answer. Had you seen the person you referred to as Milan Lukic before, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are just having trouble hearing you. And the other soldier that you've referred to, can you describe how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, the same way. He was wearing this same clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these men enter the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: In the middle of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you see where Milan Lukic and this other soldier were when Sredoje Lukic entered the middle of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: In the hall way. Near the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've said that there were other people outside. Are you able to approximate how many people were outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Another three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened in the house at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: He cleared the table and said, "Put your money to one side and your jewellery to the other." He took out a knife and said, "If we find a penny on anyone," he turned the blunt side of his knife and said that he would use it. And that he would search us all later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who are you referring to when you say "he"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the people comply with his demand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. Anybody who had any money or jewellery on them, they just didn't have to take their earrings out of their ears, if they had any. A man, a relative of mine, whose name was [redacted], had a ring, a rather large ring, and he said, "Give me that ring." And he put it on his own hand. And when the people had put all their money and jewellery, valuables, on the table, I did so too, what little I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, he -- who are you referring to when you say "he" when you speak about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is him that is talking to (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people crying at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, people were crying, the girls were crying. He said that we should clear the room so that they could all strip and be examined, searched. A soldier I didn't know was sitting in an armchair in that empty room, and the people went in three by three. And my turn came too. I went into the house with two of my neighbours. He asked us whether we had any money or anything else, whether our mother had given us some money, we said no. I said no. And then we went out. And that's how all the people were searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person who was sitting in the chair, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was. He had a rifle, an automatic rifle on his knee. It was an armchair rather than a chair. And he swung to and fro on the armchair and his rifle was cocked -- across his knees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you made to take your clothes off in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other people that were in the room with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Everybody had to take their clothes off, the girls, the elderly, men and women, everyone. The girls were crying. The older women said -- advised them to take their clothes off and said that otherwise --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Otherwise what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Otherwise they would be killed, the young women. Because for every mistake they would take up a rifle or knife, and ... I went back to the kitchen where I was before. Sredoje Lukic took everything from the table, the gold and the money. He put the money in one bag and the jewellery in the other, and he told the people, "Off we go to have a drink now. And nobody will touch you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point in time, is it daylight or night-time outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time the men or Sredoje Lukic says, "We are going to drink now." Is it daytime or night-time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Day, day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did all of this take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, it lasted about an hour and a half, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see some young women taken out of the house that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, yes, they took them out to in front of the door. But they came back quickly. What they said to them, I don't know, because there were a lot of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Sredoje Lukic said that he was going to go get something to drink, did he leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Milan Lukic and the other soldier inside the house leave at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the men that you heard outside of the house, were you able to tell whether they left too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, together with them. You could hear them until they went out. Then they switched the motor on and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the same car with the muffler missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, an exhaust pipe, muffler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. When it became dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had it been dark, or how long after sunset would you approximate it was when they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, about two and a half hours. We heard shooting at the end of the settlement, and the same vehicle which came up to in front of the door, we heard, because we heard the same exhaust pipe. It made the same noise. It was very noisy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said you heard shooting at the edge of the settlement, would that be the edge of the settlement closest to Visegrad or further away from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I said, yes, the street begins about 150 metres in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the shooting --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: About 150 metres away from that house, that's where the street is, that's where it begins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the direction from where you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: From the direction of the road. That road that they had come by, the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the direction closer to Visegrad from the house or was it further away from Visegrad, going away from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It was 150 metres from the house, very close by. I don't know if it was further or nearer, but 150 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of that car get closer to the house that you were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that car stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did it stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after the sound of the car stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: They got out and told the people that we would have to move, to go to another house, that we weren't safe where we were. They said that allegedly the Green Berets were shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," were you able to recognise any of the people that came to the house this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. It was the same people who had looted us, who were in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: We moved to the second house. All the people had to leave the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. first house, Memic's house, and go to the other house that was nearer to the creek, the house by the creek because allegedly the Green Berets were shelling and shooting and attacking the town and they said we weren't safe there. I was one of the last to leave the house. There was some light coming but there was not a lot of light, and their flashlights. When we came in front of the second house, by the entrance, by the door, the same man was standing there with a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the name -- do you know the name of that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic, who introduced himself, who said Sredoje Lukic was his name when he looted us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you at the time when you're leaving the first house, the Memic house. Did you have your shoes on at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, I put one shoe on, but I couldn't find the other shoe in the dark. So I put something else on to go to that other house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You put on somebody else's shoe on your other foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I came to that house. I passed several of their soldiers on that part of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a few moments ago you mentioned flashlights. Can you tell us approximately how many flashlights you recall seeing that day, or that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, two or three perhaps. I'm giving you an approximation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was holding those flashlights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: They were. I didn't dare look at them, let alone anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the soldiers that had returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. The soldiers. It was their flashlight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they shining those flashlights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: On to the road, so that nobody should leave the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your mother at the time that you left the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: She had gone on in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close was she to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Very close, but I can't be specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have been able to touch her if you wanted to? Were you that close?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No, no, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, taking you back to the time that you're about to enter this house by the creek, you told us that you saw Sredoje Lukic at that point. Can you tell us where precisely you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: At the entrance, standing at the doorway. And he patted me on the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you look at him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Nothing. He just smiled and patted me on the shoulder, and I looked at his bombs, the one he had -- the ones he had around his belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you're referring to as bombs? Had you seen anything similar to this before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, on television before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the last person to enter the house that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Perhaps there was someone else, several others, but I was towards the end of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you entered the house, was the door closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes, locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that it was locked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: I heard the key being turned in the lock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what you remember about the inside of that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, it looked -- how do you mean? Whether it was furnished or that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what, if any, furniture was in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: There was a table in the middle where I sat, several sofas, a kitchen table in the middle of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there light in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see where your mother was inside that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there sufficient light for you to be able to see her face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: No, just heard her voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe for us the state or the state of mind of the people in the room at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: It was overcrowded. When I went in, I sat on the table straightaway. The children were crying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people appear scared to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear anything from outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. We could hear some sort of laughing and joking around, that kind of thing, in front of the house. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel that something dangerous was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your mother at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: She was on the sofa underneath the window, by the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away were you from her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Four metres perhaps. I'm always giving you approximations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time hear your mother tell some of the people in the house that she had a headache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG84
utterances.text: Yes. To a woman, a neighbour, she said she had a headache and could she move to the window? And that's what she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest this as a place to pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume tomorrow morning at 9.30. If Dr. De Grave comes at an appropriate time where we could interrupt the witness's evidence, we will take his, but otherwise, I'm afraid he'll just have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll suggest to him he be here at 9.30. If he is here at 9.30, will we take him then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. We will take him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now to 9.30 tomorrow.
